items.painDesc: 3 to 5 seconds is a recipe for losing Google rankings and up to 50% of visitors.

items.painDesc: 80 to 120 PLN/month forever, vendor lock-in, limited customisation.
items.solutionDesc: After launch ~10 PLN/month for hosting and domain. No subscriptions, full control.

items.pain: An old WordPress that barely runs?
items.painDesc: Plugins break, the site is slow, the admin gets attacked, endless updates.
items.solutionDesc: I will speed it up, secure it and maintain it. Or migrate to a modern stack while preserving Google rankings.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Did not find an answer to your question? Please feel free to get in touch directly.

items.q: How much does a website cost?
items.a: A business landing page costs PLN 349. Larger projects are quoted individually following an initial conversation. Every client receives a complete quote before work begins, with no hidden costs.

A business landing page is delivered within 48 hours of finalising requirements and receiving the materials (logo, copy, photographs). Larger projects typically take 1 to 4 weeks. Timelines are set realistically and consistently met.

items.q: Are hosting and domain included in the price?
items.a: Hosting and domain are not included in the base price. Hosting is available as an add-on (from PLN 199 per year), and the domain can be purchased separately (typically PLN 50 to 150 per year, depending on the extension). Deployment to client-owned hosting is also possible.

items.q: Can I edit the content myself after launch?
items.a: Yes. Training on editing the key sections of the website is available as an add-on after launch. Implementation of a CMS panel (for example for blog management) is delivered as part of a custom quote.

items.q: Do you also handle SEO optimisation?
items.a: Yes. Every project includes basic SEO optimisation (meta tags, sitemap, structured data, Core Web Vitals). Advanced ranking work and content marketing are offered as separate services.

New websites are built with Next.js, React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS. They are fast, well-indexed by Google and easy to extend further. I also know WordPress and can maintain, fix, speed up or migrate away from it if you already have a site on that platform. The technology choice always reflects the specific project requirements.

items.q: Will the website be accessible to people with disabilities?
items.a: Every project follows accessibility best practices: semantic HTML, proper contrast, readable fonts, keyboard navigation and alt text for images. Full WCAG 2.1 AA compliance (audit, ARIA, screen reader testing with NVDA and VoiceOver, form field labels) is available as an add-on. For public sector deployments I deliver a full WCAG audit and compliance with the digital accessibility act.
